title: Tokyo vs Osaka: Which Should You Visit?

faqs.question: Is Tokyo or Osaka better for first-time visitors to Japan?
faqs.answer: Both are excellent for first-timers, but they offer different experiences. Tokyo is the quintessential mega-city — skyscrapers, world-class museums, the best metro on Earth, and every cuisine imaginable. faqs.question: How far apart are Tokyo and Osaka?
faqs.answer: About 500 km. The Shinkansen bullet train takes 2 hours 22 minutes (Nozomi) or about 3 hours (Hikari). A reserved Nozomi seat costs ¥13,870 (~$93) one way. The Japan Rail Pass covers the Hikari but not the Nozomi. Budget alternatives include overnight buses (¥3,000–6,000, 8–9 hours) and Peach/Jetsta

faqs.question: Is it worth visiting both Tokyo and Osaka?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. With 7+ days in Japan, most travelers split time between both cities. A common split is 4 days Tokyo + 3 days Osaka (with day trips to Kyoto and Nara). The cities complement each other — Tokyo for its scale and modernity, Osaka for its street food and warmth. Fly into one and out of the

faqs.question: Which is cheaper, Tokyo or Osaka?
faqs.answer: Osaka is noticeably cheaper — roughly 20–30% less for accommodation and 15–20% less for dining. Mid-range hotels in Osaka run ¥7,000–14,000/night vs ¥10,000–20,000 in Tokyo. Street food in Osaka is legendary and cheap (takoyaki ¥500, okonomiyaki ¥800). Budget meals cost about the same in both cities

faqs.question: Is Osaka friendlier than Tokyo?
faqs.answer: Yes — this is one of the most consistent observations from travelers. Osakans are famously outgoing, humorous, and approachable compared to the more reserved Tokyoites. faqs.question: How many days do you need in Tokyo vs Osaka?
faqs.answer: Minimum 3 full days in Tokyo (ideally 4–5) and 2–3 days in Osaka. Tokyo has virtually unlimited things to do. faqs.question: Should I visit Tokyo or Osaka first?
faqs.answer: Whichever airport you fly out of should be your last city. Most international flights use Narita/Haneda (Tokyo) or Kansai International (Osaka).
